description: Use original CSV ranks for directional, union, and independent snapshot analysis scopes.

userStories.title: Scope ranks and winners by direction
userStories.description: As an analyst, I want gains scoped by new rank and losses by old rank so relevant movements remain eligible.
acceptanceCriteria: Use original RankingRecord.rank <= N: new for climbers and score winners, old for droppers and score losers.
Include within-top-N movements, filter before sorting and output truncation, skip missing counterparts, and leave omitted scope unrestricted without a score floor.
userStories.notes: Completed and independently reviewed. Initial directional regressions failed before implementation. Final verification: 14 unittest tests pass, including Melmetal 79->7 and score/rank direction divergence; configured mypy passes on 11 source files; Ruff lint and formatting pass. Reviewed processor and Makefile diffs; no actionable logic defects found. Existing unrelated work preserved.

userStories.title: Compare movesets across the rank-scope union
userStories.description: As an analyst, I want move changes for either snapshot top N so former top entries remain visible.
acceptanceCriteria: Union old and new records with original rank <= N; compare each matching entry once in new-rank order.
Handle missing counterparts safely, ignore charged ordering, truncate after comparison, and preserve CLI fallback 50.
userStories.notes: Completed and independently reviewed. Union, rank ordering, truncation, and CLI fallback regressions failed before implementation and now pass; charged-order and missing-counterpart cases covered. Final configured mypy, Ruff lint/format, and all 14 unittest tests pass. No actionable logic defects found.

userStories.title: Scope type totals independently by rank
userStories.description: As an analyst, I want each season independently scoped by CSV rank so type totals reflect its own top N.
acceptanceCriteria: Scope each snapshot by original rank <= N, including entries without counterparts in their own totals.
Credit full scores to each distinct dual type, impose no score floor, and preserve unrestricted omitted scope.
userStories.notes: Completed and independently reviewed. Independent totals and truncation regressions failed before implementation and now pass; distinct dual types, absent counterparts, unrestricted defaults, and scores below 80 covered. Final configured mypy, Ruff lint/format, and all 14 unittest tests pass. No actionable logic defects found.

userStories.title: Document semantics and generate all league reports
userStories.description: As a user, I want accurate usage documentation and regenerated reports for all four processors in all three leagues.
acceptanceCriteria: Update README, CLI help, docstrings, and Makefile comments only; preserve functional build settings.
Run unittest, CLI help, Make dry-run, and 12 explicit fail-fast processor/league generations using Python 3.11+; create only new timestamped reports.
Review scoped diff and report check limitations; never mark stories passed without required typecheck evidence.
userStories.notes: Completed after US-001 through US-003. README, help, docstrings, and Makefile comments updated; diff review confirms functional Makefile settings unchanged. Independent review identified stale tooling documentation, now corrected to describe pyproject.toml. Final checks: 14 unittest tests, configured mypy on 11 source files, Ruff lint and formatting on 12 files, CLI help, Make dry-run, and git diff --check pass. Implementation generated 12 reports with separately checked exit 0 using Python 3.11, scope 100, output 25, min delta 0.1 (ranks 1). Great winners timestamp 20260907-222628; other reports 20260907-222629. Review confirmed all 12 reports exist and spot-checked Melmetal and old-top-N moveset entries. No commits or branch operations; branchName is metadata only.
